events.title: The Cracked Floor
events.bodyText: A hairline crack has appeared in the bunker's concrete sub-floor, and damp grit darkens the seam. Aris Thorne runs his fingers along it with the precision of a man who designed shelters like this before the war. 'This needs a proper inspection,' he says quietly. 'I know what a warning like this can mean.'

choices.text: Let Aris assess the damage fully.

events.title: The Overwork
events.bodyText: Aris hasn't slept in three days. His hands shake as he mixes concrete, but his work is flawless. Other survivors whisper that he's killing himself. When approached, he snaps: 'I designed these shelters. Every crack is my fault. Let me fix it.'

choices.text: Force Aris to rest. The repair holds. It's good enough.
Let him push through. He knows what he's doing.

events.title: The Resolution
events.bodyText: The crack is sealed. Aris stands in front of his work, one hand pressed against the concrete. 'My daughter would have turned seven today,' he says. 'She would have been proud of this.' He turns away from the wall. Some cracks can't be filled with concrete.

events.title: The Signal
events.bodyText: Maya Lin freezes at the radio console. Her hand hovers over the frequency dial. 'That pattern,' she whispers. 'It resembles an old emergency message format. But the voice — ' She presses the headphones tighter. 'It sounds like my brother's. Jakob was stationed at Checkpoint Kilo.'

choices.text: Help Maya trace the signal to its source.

events.title: The Death Loop
events.bodyText: The apparent signal source is an automated transmitter running on a failing battery. The recording may be three years old; Maya cannot prove when Jakob made it or what became of him. She removes the headphones. Her face is completely still. 'If he was alone,' she says, 'he died talking to a radio.'

choices.text: Help Maya channel her grief into saving others through the radio.
Give Maya space. She needs to process this alone.

events.title: The Broadcast
events.bodyText: Maya sits at the radio console, her hand steady on the transmitter. 'This is Free Radio, broadcasting from a shelter still standing,' she says. The signal is short-range and the ash swallows parts of it, but her voice gets through. 'If you can hear this, you're not alone.' Somewhere nearby, a few survivors press their headphones tighter.

events.title: The Refugee Mass
events.bodyText: A woman and two children huddle in the airlock, their dosimeter readings screaming. They have twenty minutes of safe exposure left. Captain Vance stands at the hatch, arms crossed. 'Rations are tight,' he says flatly. 'Every mouth we add shortens our survival window by days. The math is clear.' The mother is crying.

events.title: The Command Decision
events.bodyText: Vance's tactical assessment is grim: accepting the refugees will put additional strain on food stores, though the exact cost depends on how many can be sheltered and for how long. The bunker has room. The youngest child — maybe four years old — is shivering so hard her teeth are chattering. Vance won't look at her. He's staring at the inventory ledger instead.

choices.text: Admit the refugees. Override Vance's recommendation.
Turn them away. Vance's cold math is correct.

events.title: The Treaty
events.bodyText: Vance removes his service pistol and sets it on the table. 'I spent ten years following orders that turned me into something I didn't recognize,' he says. 'Today, I'm giving a different order.' He extends his hand — to a Militia commander, to a Garrison defector, to anyone willing to stop fighting long enough to survive.

events.title: The ARS Diagnosis
events.bodyText: Dr. Rostov reviews the bloodwork with clinical detachment. 'The results are consistent with severe acute radiation injury,' she says. 'I cannot give a reliable timetable without more observation.' The patient is someone she's treated before — someone she knows by name. Her voice doesn't shake. Her hands do.

choices.text: Review the treatment options with Elena.

events.title: The Triage
events.bodyText: Elena lays out the cost in a monotone: 'A large share of our remaining medical supplies. Antibiotics, analgesics, iodine, surgical kits — resources we may need elsewhere, for a patient with uncertain odds.' She pauses. 'The mathematics is clear.' The patient is watching her. Waiting.

choices.text: Save the patient. Every life matters regardless of cost.
Trust Elena's clinical judgment. Let them pass peacefully.

events.title: The Remedy
events.bodyText: In the quiet of the medical bay, Elena holds a vial up to the lantern light. The liquid inside catches a faint green reflection — an experimental compound derived from nursery spores. 'The Ash Rot preparation,' she whispers. 'It took me three years to make. It may help with chronic fallout lung damage, but we still need controlled trials.' She labels the vial. One word: 'HOPE.'

events.title: The Defector's Story
events.bodyText: A Garrison soldier stumbles into the airlock, uniform torn, rifle empty. 'I couldn't do it anymore,' they gasp. 'The executions. The tribute collections. Colonel Voss ordered us to burn a settlement that was three days late on food quotas. I — I walked away. They're probably hunting me.' They hand over a data chip. 'Patrol routes. Supply schedules. Everything I know.'

choices.text: Welcome the defector. Their intel is invaluable.
Take the intel but turn them away. Too dangerous.

events.title: The Prophet Sighting
events.bodyText: A traveler at the Grain Exchange repeats a frightening claim: 'I saw The Vessel — the Cult's prophet. Walking through Reactor Site 4 as if it were a garden. I never saw a suit or checked the reading myself. The Geiger counter was screaming and they were just... walking. Smiling.' The traveler's hands are shaking. 'They said to tell everyone: the Clear World is coming.'

choices.text: Send someone to verify. If it's true, we need to know.

events.title: The Council Invitation
events.bodyText: A Militia courier arrives with a handwritten letter. 'The Ash Militia Council requests the presence of a representative from your shelter at our monthly assembly. Proposed topics include mutual defense, water purification methods, and whether a formal trade route is practical. Food and lodging are offered. Weapons checked at the door.' The letter is signed by twelve different hands.

choices.text: Send a representative. This could be the start of something.
Decline. We can't afford to send anyone right now.
